outcome: criterion not met: no GSP01 gate is registered; SP01 closes without change
consequence: RELAY_READAHEAD_POLICY stays upstream (the gsp02-v4 default). The byte-based window policy stays in the code behind its switch, unmeasured as a gate. This probe is descriptive evidence only and its data are never pooled into a gate.
analysis: Problem present: C0 has a mean start-phase stall time >= 1 s in 5 of 12 cells, all in the mixed profile (mixed/1MiB/30Mbit C0 4.59 / W16 3.86 / W32 3.84; mixed/4MiB/30Mbit C0 1.88 / W16 0.65 / W32 3.06; mixed/16MiB/30Mbit C0 3.13 / W16 0.0 / W32 3.46; mixed/1MiB/60Mbit C0 7.53 / W16 2.69 / W32 5.07; mixed/4MiB/60Mbit C0 3.03 / W16 0.78 / W32 5.54 s). Fast and thin cells do not stall with C0.

W16 halves the mean stall time in 4 of the 5 problem cells, but its mean time_to_start_s is more than 2 s above C0's in mixed/16MiB/60Mbit (mixed/16MiB/60Mbit C0 25.9 / W16 29.48 / W32 34.02 s), so the pre-registered criterion fails for W16. W32 halves no problem cell and has the start cost in fast/1MiB/60Mbit, mixed/16MiB/60Mbit. With 2 runs per arm and cell the start-cost cell may be noise (gsp10-v2 saw series means up to 4.1 s apart in that cell), but the rule was fixed before the run and is applied as written.

Descriptive, supporting the SP01 throughput hypothesis in one cell only: in mixed/1MiB/60Mbit the live policy delivers below the bitrate (mixed/1MiB/60Mbit C0 6.63 / W16 9.24 / W32 8.84 MB/s against 7.5 MB/s needed; C0 10 stalls per run, buffer median 1.21 s). Elsewhere delivery is at the bitrate in every arm (fast about 11.0 MB/s for 60 Mbit/s plus the buffer fill, thin and mixed/30 about 4.6-5.5 MB/s).

Side effects seen in the window arms (descriptive): the seek resume is slower by more than 2 s in mixed/1MiB/30Mbit, mixed/4MiB/60Mbit, thin/1MiB/30Mbit, thin/4MiB/30Mbit, thin/16MiB/30Mbit (mixed/1MiB/30Mbit C0 1.71 / W16 5.49 / W32 0.05; mixed/4MiB/60Mbit C0 1.43 / W16 9.35 / W32 0.05; thin/1MiB/30Mbit C0 1.76 / W16 7.57 / W32 8.53; thin/4MiB/30Mbit C0 2.56 / W16 7.32 / W32 8.52; thin/16MiB/30Mbit C0 9.02 / W16 10.28 / W32 11.36 s); 3 seek reads timed out, all in window arms and 16 MiB cells (W16 mixed/16MiB/60Mbit, W32 mixed/16MiB/30Mbit, W16 thin/16MiB/30Mbit), against 0 in C0; those runs have no resume time, so the seek means above leave out the worst cases. W16 also stalls where C0 does not (thin/1MiB/30Mbit C0 0.0 / W16 1.86 / W32 4.19 s; fast/16MiB/60Mbit C0 0.0 / W16 0.43 / W32 0.0 s).

The window arms fill the 30 s buffer faster in the fast profile (time_to_full_buffer_s, fast/1MiB/60Mbit C0 [39.585, 40.346], W16 [25.717, 29.985]), but C0 does not stall in any fast cell, so the faster fill buys nothing measurable there; the window arms even stall briefly in two fast cells (fast/4MiB/60Mbit C0 0.0 / W16 0.0 / W32 0.73 s; fast/16MiB/60Mbit C0 0.0 / W16 0.43 / W32 0.0 s).

unused_downloaded_bytes is seed bytes sent minus bytes the client received. At 60 Mbit/s the start phase (60 s of playback plus up to 30 s of buffer) reads past the seek target, the middle of the 1 GiB file, so the seek re-reads bytes already counted and the value can go negative (4 arm-cells, all at 60 Mbit/s). It is reported but not interpreted. CPU and memory are within a few percent and tens of MiB between arms; 0 app tracebacks; app error lines per run: 1 in every arm, C0 included.

A narrower hypothesis for later, not tested and not registered: a window measured in bytes helps only where pieces are small and the bitrate is high (1 MiB at 60 Mbit/s, where 4 pieces are 4 MiB, about 0.5 s of video). A candidate would also have to remove the slower seek resume seen above, whose cause is not diagnosed.
